paragraphs: In this Form 10-K, references to "Empire", the "Company", "we", "our", and "us" refer to Empire Petroleum Corporation and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, unless context indicates otherwise.

Empire Petroleum Corporation is an independent energy company that engages in unlocking value in developed assets. Empire operates primarily from the following wholly-owned subsidiaries in its areas of operations:
● Empire New Mexico LLC ("Empire New Mexico") ● Empire North Dakota LLC ("Empire North Dakota")
● Empire Texas LLC ("Empire Texas") ● Empire Louisiana LLC ("Empire Louisiana")

Empire was incorporated in the state of Delaware in 1985. The consolidated financial statements of Empire Petroleum Corporation and subsidiaries include the accounts of the Company and its wholly-owned subsidiaries.

Our mission is to increase shareholder value by building oil and natural gas reserves in strategic plays in the United States. To accomplish our mission, we plan to execute the following business strategies:
● Cost-effectively optimize well production ● Reduce unit operating costs and improve margins
● Target proved developed producing acquisitions in predictable fields that have historically had low production decline and long lives
● Focus on high-quality assets that add scale and provide synergies to our existing portfolio and core areas of operation
We operate as a single operating segment. For additional information, see Note 17 – Segment Reporting of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.

Our Annual Report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K and all amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Exchange Act, as well as proxy statements and other information we file with, or furnish to, the SEC are available free of charge on our website at www.empirepetroleumcorp.com. We make these documents available as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file them with, or furnish them to, the SEC. The information contained on our website, or available by hyperlink from our website, is not incorporated into this Form 10-K or other documents we file with, or furnish to, the SEC. We intend to use our website as a means of disclosing material non-public information and for complying with our disclosure obligations under Regulation Fair Disclosure. Such disclosures will be included on our website in the "Investor Relations" sections. Accordingly, investors should monitor such portions of our website, in addition to following our press releases, SEC filings and public conference calls and webcasts.

In addition, we use social media to communicate with our investors and the public about our company, our businesses and our results of operations. The information we post on social media could be deemed to be material information. Therefore, we encourage investors, the media and others interested in our company to review the information we post on the social media channels listed in the "Investor Relations" section of our website.

We are an independent operator in four geographic areas in the United States. For our operated properties, we manage and influence production using a combination of experienced field personnel and third-party service providers to execute our mission. Our producing properties have reasonably predictable production profiles and cash flows, subject to commodity price and cost fluctuations. As is common in the industry in which we operate, we selectively participate in drilling and developmental activities in non-operated properties. Decisions to participate in non-operated properties are made after technical and economic analysis of the projects which also considers the operating expertise and historical track record of the operators.

Empire New Mexico includes approximately 709 gross (525 net) wells on 48,000 gross (41,000 net) acres in Lea County, New Mexico. We also have 18 royalty interest ("RI") wells with an average overriding royalty interest ("ORRI") of 0.6%. Empire New Mexico's assets primarily produce oil with accompanying natural gas and NGLs production. Empire New Mexico's properties are located in Grayburg/San Andres (primary source of production), Queen-Seven Rivers-Yates, Devonian, Abo, Blineberry, Tubb, and Drinkard formations.

headings: The Standardized Measure of estimated reserves may not be accurate estimates of the current fair value of estimated proved oil and natural gas reserves.
Estimates of proved reserves and future net cash flows are not precise. The actual quantities of our proved reserves and future net cash flows may prove to be lower than estimated.
Unless reserves are replaced, production and estimated reserves will decline, which may adversely affect our financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows.
New technologies may cause our exploration and development methods to become obsolete, causing an adverse effect on our production.
We have indebtedness and may incur substantially more debt. Higher levels of indebtedness make us more vulnerable to economic downturns and adverse business developments.

Our business requires substantial capital expenditures. Management may be unable to obtain needed capital or financing on satisfactory terms or at all, which could lead to a decline in oil and natural gas reserves.
The loss or unavailability of capital provided by our two largest stockholders could have a material adverse effect on our business.
We may not be able to generate cash to service all of our indebtedness and may be forced to take other actions to satisfy our obligations.

A negative shift in stakeholder sentiment towards the oil and natural gas industry and increased attention to ESG matters and conservation matters could adversely affect our ability to raise equity and debt capital.
General Operations
Liquidity and capital constraints could adversely affect our operations and financial conditions.
Competition for assets, materials, people and capital can be significant.

Our producing properties and proved reserves are concentrated in New Mexico, North Dakota, Montana, Texas, and Louisiana, making us vulnerable to risks associated with operating in limited major geographic areas.
A significant portion of our oil, natural gas, and NGLs sales are concentrated in only a few purchasers, which increases our exposure to substantial sales interruptions.
Our insurance policies may not adequately protect us against certain unforeseen risks.
Hedging transactions may expose us to risk of financial loss or limit participation in commodity price increases and involve other risks.
If forecasted prices for oil, natural gas, and NGLs decrease, we may be required to take significant future write-downs of the financial carrying values of our properties in the future.
We are subject to various environmental risks, and governmental regulation relating to environmental matters.
Acquisitions involve a number of risks, including the risk that we will discover unanticipated liabilities or other problems associated with the acquired business or property.
We may not realize an adequate return on oil and natural gas investments.
We operate or participate in oil and natural gas leases with third-parties who may not be able to fulfill their commitments to our projects.
We could be adversely affected by increased costs of service providers utilized by us.
Our ability to use our existing net operating loss carryforwards or other tax attributes could be further limited.
The credit risk of our counterparties could adversely affect us.
Unexpected events could disrupt our business and adversely affect our results of operations.
paragraphs: Our operations are subject to various risks and uncertainties in the ordinary course of business. The following summarizes significant risks and uncertainties that may adversely affect our operations or financial position. Risks and uncertainties discussed below are not a comprehensive listing of those faced by us. Additional risks not presently known or that are deemed immaterial may also affect us. Readers should carefully consider the risk factors included below and other information included and incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Standardized Measure is a reporting convention that provides a common basis for comparing oil and natural gas companies subject to the rules and regulations of the SEC. This measure requires the use of operating and development costs prevailing as of the date of computation. Consequently, it will not reflect the prices ordinarily received or that will be received for oil and natural gas production because of varying market conditions, nor may they reflect the actual costs that will be required to produce or develop the oil and natural gas properties. Accordingly, estimates included in this report of future net cash flows may be materially different from the future net cash flows that are ultimately received. In addition, the 10 percent discount factor, which is required by the rules and regulations of the SEC to be used in calculating discounted future net cash flows for reporting purposes, may not be the most appropriate discount factor based on interest rates in effect from time to time and risks associated with us or the oil and natural gas industry in general. Therefore, the Standardized Measure included in this report should not be construed as an accurate estimate of the current market value of our proved reserves.

Numerous uncertainties exist in estimating quantities of proved reserves and future net cash flows therefrom. Estimates of proved reserves and related future net cash flows are based on various assumptions, which may ultimately prove to be inaccurate. Petroleum engineering is a subjective process of estimating accumulations of oil and natural gas that cannot be measured in an exact manner. paragraphs: The following is a brief listing of developments during the year ended December 31, 2025. Additional information including subsequent events may be found elsewhere in this report.

On May 1, 2025, the Company extended its option to purchase certain New Mexico interests from Energy Evolution to allow for payment for such extension to be made in cash in lieu the issuance of the 16,800 shares of common stock. The Company made a cash payment to Energy Evolution on September 30, 2025 to extend the purchase option for an additional year (Note 3).

On June 17, 2025, the Company issued a promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of $4.0 million to Mr. Mulacek who immediately advanced $2.0 million under the note. The Company may request in writing that Mr. Mulacek advance up to another $2.0 million to the Company from time to time during the period beginning 45 days and ending 90 days after June 17, 2025. The note accrues interest at 5.5% and may be repaid without penalty or premium prior to the maturity date of June 17, 2027. Per the terms of the note, in the event that the Company closes a sale of its equity, the Company shall promptly, but in no event later than five business days after receipt of the proceeds, repay the lesser of (a) the initial $2.0 million advanced (including any interest or fees thereon) or (b) the amount of the equity sale to Mr. Mulacek. In the event the Company receives proceeds from the sale of any of its equity after an initial equity sale repayment and any subsequent advance, the Company shall use such proceeds to promptly repay such subsequent advance, and all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, to Mr. Mulacek. In August 2025, Empire completed an equity sale further described in Note 9 and repaid the outstanding note balance and all accrued and unpaid interest (Note 7).

On June 18, 2025, the Company entered into the second amendment to the revolver loan agreement with Equity Bank. The amendment added Empire Texas Development LLC as a third borrower and extends the obligation security by liens on substantially all of the assets of Empire Texas Development LLC (Note 7).

In August 2025, Empire completed a subscription rights offering which raised gross proceeds of $2.5 million. Empire distributed at no charge to holders of its common stock, as of the close of business on July 10, 2025 (the record date), one non-transferable subscription right for each whole share of common stock owned by that stockholder on the record date. Each subscription right entitled a rights holder to purchase one unit at a subscription price equal to $0.07367 per unit, each unit consisting of 0.0139 shares of the Company's common stock and one rights warrant to purchase 0.0136 shares of the Company's common stock equal to $5.46 per whole share. No fractional shares of common stock are issued in the rights offering, including upon exercise of the warrants. The subscription rights were initially set to expire if they were not exercised or extended at the discretion of the Company by July 25, 2025; however, this date was subsequently extended to August 20, 2025. The warrants expired 90 days after August 20, 2025 (Note 9).

On September 24, 2025, the Company issued a convertible promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of $4.0 million to Mr. Mulacek and advanced an initial $2.0 million payable in full on September 23, 2027. An additional $2.0 million may be advanced from time to time from March 23, 2026 and for a period of six months thereafter. The note accrues interest at 5.5% and may be repaid without penalty or premium prior to the maturity date. At the discretion of Mr. Mulacek all or any portion of the outstanding principal amount of the note may be converted into shares of common stock at a conversion price of $4.27 per share, subject to customary adjustments up to a maximum conversion shares amount of 936,768. As partial consideration for the note, the Company issued Mr. Mulacek a warrant certificate to purchase up to 281,030 common shares at a $4.27 exercise price which will expire on September 24, 2028. (Note 7).

On November 5, 2025, the note was amended to change the conversion price of the initial $2.0 million advance to $4.32 per share for a maximum conversion shares amount of 462,962 and to provide that any further advances are at the discretion of Mr. Mulacek. The warrant certificate was also amended to change the exercise price to $4.32 and the maximum shares available for purchase to 138,889 (Note 7).

On December 10, 2025, the Company entered into a letter agreement to acquire the remaining 40% of certain New Mexico interests from Energy Evolution which was finalized subsequent to December 31, 2025. As consideration, Empire issued 562,500 shares of common stock on January 5, 2026, which is the closing date of the letter agreement, based on an agreed upon price of $3.20 per share for an aggregate agreed upon value of $1.8 million (Note 3).

On December 29, 2025, the Company entered into the third amendment to the revolver loan agreement with Equity Bank. The amendment preserved the maximum revolver commitment amount of $20.0 million and extended the maturity date to December 29, 2028 (Note 7).

paragraphs: 本Form 10-K中，提及「Empire」、「本公司」、「我們」、「我們的」及「我們」，係指Empire Petroleum Corporation及其全部出資之子公司，除非文意另有說明。
Empire Petroleum Corporation為一獨立能源公司，從事於成熟資產中創造價值。本公司主要透過以下全部出資之子公司於其營運區域進行營運：
● Empire New Mexico LLC（"Empire New Mexico"） ● Empire North Dakota LLC（"Empire North Dakota"）
● Empire Texas LLC（"Empire Texas"） ● Empire Louisiana LLC（"Empire Louisiana"）
本公司於1985年在德國緬因州註冊成立。本公司及其子公司之合併財務報表包含本公司及其全部出資之子公司之帳戶。
本公司之目標為透過於美國戰略性油氣田建立油氣儲備，以提升股東價值。為達成此目標，本公司計畫執行以下業務策略：
● 以成本效益方式優化井之生產 ● 減少單位營運成本並提高毛利率
● 選擇具備可預測性且歷史生產遞減率低且壽命長之已開發生產油田進行買賣
● 關注高品質資產，這些資產能增加規模並為我們現有資產組合及核心業務領域帶來協同效益
我們以單一營運分部運作。如需更多資訊，請參閱財務會計彙編附註第 17 節 – 分部報告。

本公司年度報告 10-K、季報 10-Q、現況報告 8-K 以及所有這些報告的修正案，均依證券交易法第 13(a) 或 15(d) 章節的規定，向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交或提供，並可在本公司網站 www.empirepetroleumcorp.com 無償取得。我們會在電子提交或提供這些文件給 SEC 後，儘速將這些文件公開。本公司網站上或透過超連結取得的資訊，並未納入本 10-K 表單或其他我們提交或提供的文件中。本公司意圖將網站作為披露重大非公開資訊及符合我們根據公平披露規則（Regulation Fair Disclosure）披露義務的途徑。這些披露資訊將包含在網站的 "投資人關係" 部分。因此，投資人應同時監測網站的這些部分，並遵循我們的 press release、SEC 檔案及公開的會議與網路簡報。
此外，我們也透過社交媒體與投資人及公眾溝通本公司、業務及營運成果。我們在社交媒體上發布的資訊可能被視為重大資訊。因此，我們鼓勵投資人、媒體及其他對本公司感興趣的人士，審閱我們在網站 "投資人關係" 部分列出的社交媒體頻道上發布的資訊。
本公司為美國四個地理區域的獨立運營者。針對我們經營的資產，我們透過經驗豐富的現場人員與第三方服務供應商組合，執行我們的任務。我們的生產資產具有合理可預測的生產曲線與現金流，但會受到商品價格與成本波動的影響。如同我們所處行業的常見做法，我們會選擇性參與非經營資產的鑽井與開發活動。參與非經營資產的決定是在技術與經濟分析後做出的，同時也會考量經營者的專業運營能力與歷史表現。

Empire New Mexico 包含約 709 口淨產量為 525 口的油井，位於新墨西哥州 Lea 縣 48,000 英畝（淨 41,000 英畝）的土地上。我們還擁有 18 口 royalty interest（"RI"）油井，平均 overriding royalty interest（"ORRI"）為 0.6%。Empire New Mexico 的資產主要生產原油，並伴隨天然氣與 NGLs 的生產。Empire New Mexico 的資產位於 Grayburg/San Andres（主要產油層）、Queen-Seven Rivers-Yates、Devonian、Abo、Blineberry、Tubb 和 Drinkard 等層位。

paragraphs: 以下為2025年12月31日財務年度期間發生之重要事項簡要清單。更多資訊及後續事件請參閱本報告其他部分。
2025年5月1日，本公司將其購買新墨西哥州權益之選擇權延長，允許以現金支付取代發行16,800股普通股。本公司於2025年9月30日以現金支付給Energy Evolution，以延長購買選擇權一年（註3）。

2025年6月17日，本公司向Mr. Mulacek發行總金額為4.0百萬美元之借款憑據，其立即根據憑據進賠2.0百萬美元。本公司可書面請求Mr. Mulacek在2025年6月17日起45日至90日間，不時進賠最多2.0百萬美元。憑據利率為5.5%，可在到期日2027年6月17日前無罰款或 premium 進行償還。根據憑據條款，若本公司完成其資本權益之銷售，本公司應於收到資金後立即，但不遲於五個營業日內，償還給Mr. Mulacek較低者（a）初始進賠2.0百萬美元（包括任何利息或費用）或（b）出售權益之金額。若本公司在初始權益銷售償還及任何後續進賠後，收到任何資本權益出售之資金，本公司應使用該資金立即償還該後續進賠，以及所有已累計且未償還之利息給Mr. Mulacek。2025年8月，Empire完成一筆權益銷售，進一步說明於註9，並償還所有未償還憑據金額及所有已累計且未償還之利息（註7）。
2025年6月18日，本公司與Equity Bank簽訂第二項信貸協議修正案。修正案增加Empire Texas Development LLC為第三借款人，並擴展擔保責任至Empire Texas Development LLC substantially all 之資產上之留置權（註7）。

2025年8月，Empire完成一筆認股權證發行，籌得總金額為2.5百萬美元。Empire於2025年7月10日（除息日）收市時，向持有其普通股之股東，每人每持有整股普通股發放一張不可轉讓之認股權證。每張認股權證允許權利持有人以每單位0.07367美元之認購價購買一單位，每單位包含本公司0.0139股普通股及一張權利權證，可購買0.0136股普通股，每整股價值5.46美元。認股權證發行不發行任何零股普通股，包括權利權證行使後。認股權證最初設定於2025年7月25日到期，若未行使或延長，但本公司隨後將此日期延長至2025年8月20日。權利權證於2025年8月20日後90日到期（註9）。

2025年9月24日，本公司向Mr. Mulacek發行一張可轉換借款憑據，總本金為4.0百萬美元，並進賠初始2.0百萬美元，於2027年9月23日償還。額外2.0百萬美元可於2026年3月23日起六個月內不時進賠。憑據利率為5.5%，可在到期日無罰款或 premium 進行償還。根據Mr. Mulacek之裁量，可將所有或部分未償還本金轉換為普通股，轉換價格為每股4.27美元，受常規調整限制，最高轉換股數為936,768股。作為部分對價，本公司向Mr. Mulacek發行一張權證，可購買最多281,030股普通股，行權價格為4.27美元，於2028年9月24日到期。（註7）。
2025年11月5日，該憑據經修正，將初始2.0百萬美元進賠之轉換價格變更為每股4.32美元，最高轉換股數為462,962股，並規定任何進一步進賠由Mr. Mulacek裁量。權證亦經修正，將行權價格變更為4.32美元，最高可購買股數變更為138,889股（註7）。
2025年12月10日，本公司與Energy Evolution簽訂一項協議，以取得其新墨西哥州權益之剩餘40%，該交易於2025年12月31日後完成。作為對價，Empire於2026年1月5日（協議終止日）發行562,500股普通股，基於每股3.20美元之協議價格，總協議價值為1.8百萬美元（註3）。

headings: 標準化測算的預估儲備量可能無法準確反映預估已證石油及天然氣儲備的當前公允價值。
已證儲備量及未來淨現金流的估計並非完全精確。我們的實際已證儲備量及未來淨現金流可能低於預估。
除非儲備量得以補充，否則產量及預估儲備量將下降，這可能會對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及/或現金流產生不利影響。
新技術可能使我們的探勘及開發方法過時，導致對我們的產量產生不利影響。
我們負有債務，並可能產生更多債務。較高的債務水平使我們更容易受到經濟衰退及不利商業發展的影響。
我們的業務需要大量資本支出。管理層可能無法以滿意的條件或完全無法取得所需資本或融資，這可能會導致石油及天然氣儲備減少。
我們的兩大股東所提供的資本若喪失或無法取得，可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
我們可能無法產生足夠現金以償付所有債務，並可能被迫採取其他行動以履行我們的義務。
對石油及天然氣產業的利害關係人情緒轉為負面，以及對環境、社會及治理（ESG）事項及保育事項的關注增加，可能會不利於我們籌集股本及債務資本的能力。
一般營運
流動性及資金限制可能會不利於我們的營運及財務狀況。
對於資產、材料、人力及資金的競爭可能相當激烈。
我們的開採資產及已證實儲備主要集中於新墨西哥州、北達科他州、蒙大拿州、德克薩斯州及路易斯安那州，使我們面臨在有限的主要地理區域營運所產生的風險。
我們的石油、天然氣及NGLs銷售收入主要集中於僅幾個買方，這會增加我們遭遇重大銷售中斷的風險。
我們的保險政策可能無法充分保護我們免於某些未預見的風險。

若預測油、天然氣及NGLs價格下降，我們可能需在未來進行重大之未來減值提列，以反映我們資產之財務帳面價值。
我們面臨各種環境風險，以及與環境事項相關之政府規範。
收購涉及多種風險，包括我們可能發現未預期之負債或其他與收購之業務或資產相關之問題。

我們可能因使用服務提供者之成本增加而受到不利影響。
我們使用現有淨營業虧損結轉或其他稅務屬性之能力可能進一步受到限制。

paragraphs: 本公司營運面臨各種風險與不確定性，這些風險與不確定性屬於日常營運的一部分。以下內容總結了可能對本公司營運或財務狀況產生不利影響的重要風險與不確定性。下列討論的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面對的全部風險。此外，尚有其他風險，可能尚未被識別或被認為不重要，也可能影響本公司。讀者應仔細考慮下列風險因素及其他資訊，並參考本年度10-K表報表所包含及引用的資訊。

標準化指標是一種報表慣例，提供一個共同的基礎，用以比較受美國證券交易委員會（SEC）規則與規範管制的油氣公司。此指標要求使用計算日期當時的營運與開發成本。因此，此指標不會反映通常所收到或將會收到的油氣產量價格，因為市場條件會有所變動，也不一定反映實際所需的生產或開發油氣資源的成本。因此，本報告中包含的未來淨現金流預估，可能與最終實際收到的未來淨現金流有重大差異。此外，10%的折現率，根據美國證券交易委員會（SEC）的規則與規範，在計算用以報表目的的折現未來淨現金流時必須使用，可能根據當時的利率與本公司或油氣產業整體的風險，並非最適當的折現率。因此，本報告中包含的標準化指標，不應被視為本公司已證實儲備的當前市場價值的準確預估。
在估算已證實儲備數量與其衍生的未來淨現金流時，存在許多不確定性。已證實儲備與相關未來淨現金流的預估，是基於各種假設，這些假設最終可能證明是不正確的。石油工程是一種主觀的估算過程，用以估算油氣積累量，無法以精確方式測量。已經濟可行回收的油氣儲備與未來淨現金流的預估，取決於許多變數因素與假設，包括以下內容：
● 歷史產量與其他產區產量之比較；
● 政府機關規範之假設影響；● 可用相關資料之品質、數量及解釋；
● 未來商品價格之假設；
